feedback: Judged from earlier races and the candidate's contents, not from any race of this candidate. Iteration 1 (base_speed 1.5, kd 0.4) is the best raced design at 170.5. It completed 2 of 20 oval runs, and every s-bend and slalom run still ended off_track with about one line-loss event each (max_error about 0.062, just past the 0.06 limit). This candidate changes only base_speed, from 1.5 to 1.3. That is a single, well-motivated step: the iteration 1 telemetry places the failure at the sharpest bend, and the iteration 0 to 1 change showed that the failure responds to controller changes. The geometry, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, kd 0.4, weights and line_loss are all unchanged, so any difference in the race can be attributed to speed. The contract is satisfied: all values are within limits and the sensor count matches the weights. The main risk is completion time. Oval finishes at 1.5 took about 1.86 s, and a drop to 1.3 scales the average speed by roughly 0.87, which should still fit the 3.0 s limit if the robot stays on the line. Read the next race as follows. If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall toward 0 and max_error drops below 0.06, but progress still stalls before the end of those tracks, the speed-limited hypothesis holds and base_speed should move back up to about 1.4 with kd 0.4 held. If line losses persist at the same bend at 1.3, the cause is not only speed, and the next change should be kd (for example 0.4 to 0.5) before any change to kp. If the oval finishes more often but completion_time rises past about 2.5 s, treat that as the trade-off and search for the speed that balances the two.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall toward 0 and max_error drops below 0.06 but progress stalls, try base_speed 1.4 with kd 0.4 held, since iteration 1 showed speed 1.5 still loses the line at the sharpest bend.

If line losses persist at 1.3, keep base_speed at 1.3 and raise kd from 0.4 to about 0.5 before touching kp, because kp 4.0 already gives a large steering range and iteration 1 improved with kd 0.2 to 0.4.
If the oval completes more often but completion_time rises above about 2.5 s, accept base_speed 1.3 as the stable point and look for a finish-time gain from the controller rather than from speed.
